ab_dune_wall.blurb: A big quartzite buttress in Jasper National Park, sitting at the foot of Mount Sorrow beside Mount Edith Cavell and looking across at Angel Glacier. Eight routes mix gear-protected and bolted lines: five trad climbs from roughly 5.7 up into the 5.10 range, plus three bolted routes around 5.10. Some lines run several pitches and have a high-mountain feel. The stone is solid, featuring incut holds, and the wall sees few visitors. The base is reached from the Edith Cavell road parking area by crossing the stream and scrambling up scree and small trees, roughly a quarter of an hour. Bring a mix of gear and expect alpine weather.

ab_shredder_reef.blurb: A small bolted crag in Jasper National Park, set up a drainage off the highway east of town. Eight sport routes sit on dark, coral-like limestone slabs, graded in the easy 5.6 to 5.7 band, so it suits newer leaders and anyone wanting low-stress mileage. The climbing is technical footwork on small holds, with sharp rock that is unkind to falls. Climbers report the lines feel alike and can get repetitive. Getting in means following the creek and passing through a short canyon with water-polished limestone that can be slippery underfoot, with the cliff appearing shortly after the canyon opens out.

ab_the_ghetto.blurb: One of the sectors at Grassi Lakes above Canmore, and the first wall you meet on the way down from the parking lot, which makes it easy to find. Seven sport routes climb slightly overhanging, demanding faces of the limestone for which Grassi is known, with grades sitting in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. There is little here for beginners. Belay spots are the steps and ledges alongside the main trail, so expect passing hikers and a social atmosphere at the base.
